Karansul

Overview

Karansul dominates trade in the city of Ingos and owns mines, sawmills and workshops. Sver describes a system of debt, low purchase prices and intimidation. When Zak obtains leverage over his hidden accounts, Karansul supplies information about Flein the Baldie and arranges a meeting. His suggestion to fetch a gold nugget from an abandoned pit conceals a dangerous trap for the inquisitive newcomer. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]

Karansul’s accounts and Baldie’s confession

Karansul first lets Baldie’s name slip while boasting that mechanical traps are better than magical ones, then denies knowing anything useful. Tilvar mentions the merchant’s mechanical grinder and the disruption caused when it breaks. Sver knows how to turn these leads into pressure. Zak first delivers the hunter’s furs to a buyer outside the merchant’s monopoly. Sver then reveals Karansul’s hidden trade and unpaid taxes, pointing to the foreman’s accounts; he also recommends Trickster as a teacher. With the accounts as leverage, Zak learns where to find Flein the Baldie, called Baldie, and secures a meeting. Evidence from the stolen collection makes the thief confess: he killed the Snoop, planted the Woodsfolk arrow and worked for a cloaked employer who knew how to evade the governor’s magical traps. [2, 3, 8, 4, 5, 9, 10, 11]

Diera and the locked mines

At the Green Clan’s new home, Grey Leaf describes the supposed man in grey as a white-haired woman. Zak identifies Diera, whose own traps protected the stolen collection. Her urgent warnings against the abandoned mines reinforce his suspicion. Tilvar explains that the governor holds the key. Karansul suggests winning it with a gold nugget and gives access to a dangerous pit, concealing the tigers that drove out its workers; Sver warns Zak of the trap. Zak obtains the nugget and presents it to the collector-governor as a business prospect. Valrasian releases the mine key, opening the way past Diera’s mercenaries. [12, 13, 14, 15, 6, 7, 16, 17]
